title: Creating 3D Objects and Shaders for my game
author: MistakeExotic6686
selftext:
no this is not a one prompt claude opus oneshot bla bla 

this took time directing how I want it to feel, teleporting it between claude and blender to fix nitpicky issues 

I know it doesn't make sense as a device its just a THING that's it

Mainly focused on nailing the shaders and feel of the look here 

Not natively generated with a 3D AI generator, this is built with threejs and exported in glb to blender

comments.author: TriggerHydrant
comments.body: Interesting! Mind sharing your full pipeline? Currently working on my own asset creation for a game

replies.author: MistakeExotic6686
replies.body:
It's a bit of a be curious mess around and find out

 but:

have something in mind to make (use pinterest for inspiration) make your own version of it (either sketch on it how u want it or describe it to claude)

grab few references for shaders if u want, they really add that aesthetic feeling 

make sure you ask claude to make settings / tweak menus

and build few tools to help you out (selecting faces / subobjects?) so you can tell claude to fix a specific object instead of it guessing - make sure you parent the objects correctly if you are thinking of animating / making buttons operable for example

(in the object above the buttons are clickable and wheel thingies are turnable)

  
yeah pretty much it, hardcore Claude Coding xd

comments.author: HappyClamOfficial
comments.body: Looks like the Gameboy. Really cool!

replies.author: MistakeExotic6686
replies.body:
Using reference photos for the shaders 

and for the 3D it's not one prompt, I try to collect few reference images and tell claude with annotations which parts to use   
then iterate on it - I build a configurator (like tweaks in Claude Design) and a selection tool (for me when I hold S I can hover over specific 3D parts to highlight to claude what to fix and how)   
and then yeah, I just try to keep steering it until I am happy   
main thing to do is not rush results, these are weird devices but they cool, the buttons are functional as well
